Resolves #22083
Related: #21586, #21033

The cut-day week contains 459 merged PRs. At 390 × 844, 92 items on the busiest day exceed the space available for the smallest existing pattern. The Home loaded the right record and drew neither the strip nor its caption. The repaired phone view displays every PR below the statement.

The Portal opts into a 2 px square with a 1 px gap through the renderer's existing `look.measures` config. The renderer first tries every existing ring and standalone layout. Only if both fail does it try the configured fallback as a standalone strip. Other consumers retain their own choice of measures. [Cut-day data PR](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/22082) · [Current release timing](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21033#issuecomment-7095200969).

Evidence: L3 (branded Chrome red/green test, live renderer state, exact candidate-data overlay and counted canvas pixels) → L3 required. The cut requires a design read and cross-family approval.

## AC Evidence

| Acceptance | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Dense phone week | At 390 × 844 the real 459-item record now paints 459 distinct occupied positions. All 185 empty positions remain empty. The dated caption fits below the grid at 12 px. The strip clears the buttons by 10 px and the bottom by 11.875 px. |
| Existing layouts | The unit suite includes a 1440 × 744 case where the ordinary 5 px standalone strip must win even though a 2 px ring could fit. A sweep of 4,752 layout inputs preserved all 2,270 previously working geometries. At 1440 × 900 the actual 12-seat desktop table retains its 6 px squares. An even smaller canvas still declines to draw. |
| Regression | The browser test reaches the real Home, sets a deterministic dense record and checks the canvas worker's item/landed counts, mode, bounds and clearance from the statement. On `aa41c1f139` it observed the items but got `mode: 'none'`; the candidate gets `strip`. The real cut record is kept in its separate data PR. |

## Deltas from ticket

The two PRs are independent. This one changes the renderer, the Portal opt-in and their tests. #22082 changes only `record-week.json` and waits for this fix.

**Glance:** `standaloneFallbackSquare` is tried only after every configured square size has failed, both with and without a ring, and only as an unringed strip. A host that doesn't set it lays out exactly as before. The unit test proves both arms. With the fallback configured, the four existing viewports lay out identically, and at 1440 × 744 with a 92-PR day the existing 5 px standalone strip still wins. At 390 × 786 with a 100-PR day, the layout is `mode: 'none'` without the fallback, which is today's blank phone hero, and a 2 px strip with the fallback, whose top sits below the statement (> 717) and whose caption fits (≤ 786). At 390 × 730 it is still `none`, so the fallback never crowds a canvas that has no room. The e2e drives the real hero at 390 × 844 with a 100-item record: every item lands, nothing touches, and the strip stays inside the canvas. Verified on `ff2b9ee9b7`: hosted CI is green (39 passed), and its unit arms carry the red and green conditions by construction.
